assistiveTechnologyTests.procedure: Follow the documented procedure and listen for the information under test.

title: French passage has no language identification
description: The field notice contains a French sentence inside an English page. The alpha variant does not mark the passage with lang, so a screen reader will pronounce it with the document language. The visible text is identical in both variants.

relatedElements.note: The control identifies the same paragraph as French.

expectedBehaviour: A passage in a different language is marked with the correct lang attribute.
actualBehaviour: The French paragraph inherits lang=en from the document.
userImpact: Screen-reader users hear French pronounced as English and may not understand the closure notice.

detection.note: The rendering is identical; only the programmatic language differs.

observed.note: Page-level axe run with tags wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a, wcag21aa and best-practice. No violation was reported; the control on the same page also passes.

manualTests: Read the notice with a screen reader and listen to the pronunciation of the French sentence.

assertions: The French paragraph has no lang attribute while html has lang=en.
tests: tests/responsive-and-state.spec.js: keeps the alpha French passage without a language

reviewStatus.note: A Playwright regression test preserves the defective behaviour and its control. That is automated reproduction, not a manual or assistive-technology observation.
